clue.text: Leaving sailor with drunk in gutter — say no more

parts.note: AB, able seaman, is the usual crossword sailor
with means and, joining things together
on can mean tipsy, a little the worse for drink

indicators.note: to utter is to say, so 'say no more' tells us to drop the utter from the end of gutter

parts.note: taken as the full word before trimming

explanation.surface: A sailor stumbles home with a drunk who is lying in the gutter, and the less said the better.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say no more' is cleverly double-edged: UTTER means say, so removing it from GUTTER leaves just G.
explanation.definitionFit: Abandoning a place is leaving it behind, a straightforward synonym in the present participle.

clue.text: Assertively but inappropriately, holy man replaces wife

indicators.note: the holy man's letters take the place of the wife's abbreviation

parts.note: done inappropriately means done wrongly
ST, short for saint, is a holy man

explanation.surface: Someone forcefully, if improperly, arranges for a priest to stand in for a wife.
explanation.definitionFit: To speak assertively is to speak forcefully and with conviction, a plain synonym.

clue.text: Dutch will produce gibberish after this generous drink

definitions.text: Dutch will produce gibberish after this
definitions.meaning: Dutch is also the setter's pseudonym

explanation.surface: The setter jokes that a big drink will leave him talking nonsense.
explanation.walkthrough: Dutch is the setter's own name, so the surface is a self-mocking confession.
explanation.definitionFit: A double is twice the standard pub measure of spirits, hence a generous drink.

clue.text: Black-and-white picture captures a legend

indicators.note: the phrase 'Black-and-white picture' holds the answer inside, spanning the end of one word and start of the next

explanation.surface: An old monochrome photograph shows a famous figure.
explanation.definitionFit: An epic is a long heroic narrative, the stuff of legend; a loose synonym.

clue.text: Coach one gripped by motor madness

indicators.note: held within, so the numeral sits inside the phrase

parts.note: car rage, like road rage, is anger at the wheel
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A coach driver is seized by a fit of fury behind the wheel.
explanation.definitionFit: A coach is a horse-drawn passenger carriage, an exact synonym.

clue.text: Party happening at the end of term

definitions.meaning: the ... Party, a main UK political party

definitions.text: happening at the end of term
definitions.meaning: childbirth, which comes when a pregnancy reaches full term

explanation.surface: A party being thrown when the school term finishes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'term' looks like a school term, but it is the term of a pregnancy.
explanation.definitionFit: Labour is the British political party, and also the process of giving birth at full term.

clue.text: Spring water emerges — life's little beginnings

indicators.note: the opening letters of the four words before it are taken

explanation.surface: Water bubbles up from a spring, the tiny first stirrings of life.
explanation.definitionFit: A well is a natural source of water rising from the ground, much like a spring.

clue.text: Observer's first to scrap short newspaper deadlines?

indicators.note: only the opening letter of Observer is wanted

parts.note: a scrap is a small bit

explanation.surface: The Observer, a Sunday paper, tells us to scrap its tight print deadlines.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deadlines' is a pun: a newspaper's death notices, and 'short' says the word is abbreviated.
explanation.definitionFit: An obituary is the paper's notice of a death, and this is its clipped form.

clue.text: Kid digs rope and hangs a criminal

indicators.note: criminal suggests something bent or wrong, so the letters are twisted out of order

explanation.surface: A young thug finds some rope and hangs a lawbreaker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kid digs' looks like a child digging; it means lodgings for children.
explanation.definitionFit: Digs is slang for lodgings, and an orphanage houses kids with no parents.

clue.text: Doctor following directions to Bury

indicators.note: the doctor's letters come after the others

parts.note: E and N, east and north, are compass directions
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification

explanation.surface: A doctor is following directions to the town of Bury.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital on Bury makes it look like the Lancashire town, but it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To entomb someone is to place them in a tomb, that is, to inter the body.

clue.text: Playing craps and loo or taking turns at the wheel — in these?

definitions.text: taking turns at the wheel — in these?

indicators.note: playing about with the letters of the two game names rearranges them

explanation.surface: Commuters gamble at dice and the card game loo while each driver takes a turn.
explanation.walkthrough: Craps is a dice game and loo an old card game, so 'Playing' fits the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: In a shared commuting scheme the members take turns to drive each other.

clue.text: IT conference?

parts.note: IT looks like information technology, but it is the old euphemism for sex; a meeting of sexes is sexual intercourse, also the word for a formal assembly

explanation.surface: A gathering of computing professionals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'IT' is slang for sex appeal or sex, so the coming together is carnal.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a formal assembly of delegates and sexual intercourse, so a meeting about 'it'.

clue.text: Pledge to finish first letter to Stephen Fry?

indicators.note: the pledge goes at the end, after the letter
only the opening letter of Stephen is taken

parts.note: to pawn something is to pledge it as security

explanation.surface: A promise to finish the first letter addressed to the broadcaster Stephen Fry.
explanation.walkthrough: Stephen Fry is a British comic and writer; here fry means young fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Fry are newly hatched fish, and spawn is the eggs and young of fish.

clue.text: German enters bearing peacekeeper's weapon

indicators.note: the German's letter goes into the middle of the other two pieces

parts.note: a bearing is one's air or manner
the UN sends peacekeeping forces

explanation.surface: A German soldier enters carrying a peacekeeper's gun.
explanation.definitionFit: An air gun fires pellets by compressed air, a kind of weapon.

clue.text: Assumed European articles were upright

parts.note: UN is French for a and DER is German for the
stood means were standing upright

explanation.surface: It was taken for granted that items from Europe stood up straight.
explanation.definitionFit: Something understood is taken for granted without being said, that is, assumed.

clue.text: Acting silly, losing head for girl

indicators.note: acting up or playing about, so the remaining letters are rearranged
the first letter of silly is dropped

explanation.surface: Someone playing the fool loses their head over a girl.
explanation.definitionFit: Lily is a girl's first name, a standard crossword use of 'girl'.

clue.text: Remove all trace of a boring language

indicators.note: boring means drilling into, so the a goes inside

parts.note: Erse is Scottish or Irish Gaelic

explanation.surface: Wipe out every sign of a dull tongue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boring' reads as dull but means drilling into.
explanation.definitionFit: To erase is to wipe out completely, leaving no trace behind.

clue.text: Flashing image?

definitions.meaning: showing one's private parts in public, an indecent showing
a single frame of photographic film

explanation.surface: A camera flash goes off to produce a picture.
explanation.definitionFit: Indecent showing of the body is a flasher's act; a photograph frame is the other sense.

clue.text: Occasionally get daddy to twist

indicators.note: only every other letter of the two words is taken, starting with the second

explanation.surface: Every so often you can get your father to dance the twist.
explanation.definitionFit: Water that eddies swirls round in a circle, so it twists.

clue.text: He married in record time -these things never last!

indicators.note: the man and marriage go inside the record and time pieces

parts.note: an EP is an extended-play record
an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: He got married in record time, and such marriages never last.
explanation.definitionFit: Ephemera are short-lived items, things meant to be transient and soon discarded.

clue.text: Small breakfast item for example has large supporter

parts.note: EG, exempli gratia, means for example
a G cup is a large bra size, a bra being a supporter

explanation.surface: A small item served at breakfast, for example, has a large stand.
explanation.definitionFit: A boiled egg is served at breakfast in a small holder made for it.

clue.text: Passing a poisoned chalice is commonplace

indicators.note: poisoned suggests the letters left are corrupted into a new order
passing on the a means leaving it out of chalice

explanation.surface: Handing someone a poisoned chalice is a routine thing to do.
explanation.walkthrough: A poisoned chalice is a gift that harms the receiver; removing A leaves CHLICE, which 'poisoned' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: A commonplace is a trite, overused remark, which is what a hackneyed phrase is.

clue.text: Mad brother blowing his top is breaking news from Yorkshire?

indicators.note: the rearranged letters split the pair of Ns apart

parts.note: read as new plus s, the plural of N for new, so two Ns

indicators.note: mad suggests the letters are jumbled
losing the top letter, so the first letter of brother goes

explanation.surface: A furious brother losing his temper is the big news story up north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blowing his top' leaves ROTHER, which 'Mad' rearranges to ORTHER; 'news' is cheekily N's, two Ns. Yorkshire is a county in the north of England.
explanation.definitionFit: Yorkshire lies in the north of England, so its people and things are of that region.

clue.text: Go after men making profit

indicators.note: the go comes after the men

parts.note: RE, the Royal Engineers, are soldiers, i.e. men
a go is a turn

explanation.surface: Chasing after men to make some money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go' looks like a verb but is the noun, a turn.
explanation.definitionFit: A return on an investment is the profit or yield it brings in.

clue.text: Was China developing a device for a power cut?

definitions.text: a device for a power cut?

indicators.note: developing means changing form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A question whether China was building something to cause blackouts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'power cut' suggests an electricity outage, but it means cutting with a powered tool.
explanation.definitionFit: A motor-driven saw with a toothed chain cuts wood by engine power.

clue.text: Ambition in Dutch Opera?

indicators.note: the answer lies inside the words Dutch Opera, across the gap

explanation.surface: A query about aspirations within Dutch opera.
explanation.definitionFit: An ambition is something one aspires to and wishes for, a close synonym.

clue.text: Swell way to say goodbye

definitions.meaning: a swell is a ridge of water moving across the sea
a gesture of the hand when parting

explanation.surface: A great way to bid farewell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swell' looks like the adjective meaning excellent, but it is the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A wave is a rolling ridge of sea water and also a hand gesture of farewell.

clue.text: Custom at orchard is offering fruit

indicators.note: the words Custom at orchard hold the answer and offer it up

explanation.surface: It is customary for the orchard to sell its produce.
explanation.definitionFit: Botanically the tomato is a fruit, being the seed-bearing part of the plant.

clue.text: Compromising her virtue to secure lead in popular Bogart film

indicators.note: the anagram holds the letter inside itself
compromising her virtue suggests corrupting it, so the letters are rearranged
the opening letter of popular is taken

explanation.surface: A popular film in which a woman's honour is compromised.
explanation.walkthrough: Up the River is a 1930 prison comedy, Humphrey Bogart's first feature film.
explanation.definitionFit: Up the River (1930) was directed by John Ford and starred Spencer Tracy and Humphrey Bogart.

clue.text: Sounded impolite and cross

indicators.note: said out loud, a word for impolite sounds like the answer

parts.note: impolite means rude

explanation.surface: Someone sounded rude and angry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cross' looks like angry, but it is a crucifix.
explanation.definitionFit: A rood is a crucifix, especially one above a church screen.
